chief_complaint: a burning feeling in the chest after eating for two weeks
hpi_details: burning sensation behind the breastbone, usually starts 30-60 minutes after eating large or fatty meals, or when lying down at night. Sometimes gets a sour, bitter taste in the back of the throat. Relieved slightly by drinking water. No difficulty swallowing, no pain on swallowing, no weight loss, no chest pain on exertion.
ideas: thinks it is indigestion from eating spicy food and late-night snacks
concerns: worried it could be a warning sign of a heart attack because his father had heart disease
expectations: wants something to stop the burning feeling and to make sure his heart is okay
social_hx: business manager, drinks occasional alcohol, former smoker (quit 5 years ago)

learning_objectives: Differentiate gastrointestinal burning (heartburn) from cardiac chest pain using clear questions
Screen for alarm symptoms (dysphagia, odynophagia, weight loss, persistent vomiting)
Use empathy to address the patient's anxiety about cardiac disease
Advise on lifestyle modifications for acid reflux (smaller meals, avoiding late eating, elevating the head of the bed)
suggested_questions: Where exactly is the burning feeling, and does it travel anywhere?
When does it typically happen? Is it related to meals or lying down?
Do you get chest pain when you walk fast or exercise?
Have you had any trouble swallowing your food or pain when swallowing?
Have you noticed any unexplained weight loss?
Given your father's history, I understand why you're worried. Have you had shortness of breath, sweating, fainting, or pain spreading to your arm, jaw, or back?
